### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**5** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **216** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **156** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **156**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **101** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **10** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a31431824958c8e789427c4db593bcf867e8e051` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `f7904c567e92c30a237086dc38320432bcf09c12` — the merge of head `461552acedd0d0070debccf845de1350d307af6b` into base `a31431824958c8e789427c4db593bcf867e8e051`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin f7904c567e92c30a237086dc38320432bcf09c12 && git checkout f7904c567e92c30a237086dc38320432bcf09c12
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin a31431824958c8e789427c4db593bcf867e8e051 461552acedd0d0070debccf845de1350d307af6b && git checkout -B drift-repro a31431824958c8e789427c4db593bcf867e8e051 && git merge --no-ff 461552acedd0d0070debccf845de1350d307af6b

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a31431824958c8e789427c4db593bcf867e8e051
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `461552acedd0d0070debccf845de1350d307af6b`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-object-extension-item.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-packaged-base-refusal.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/meta-object-extension-item-door-fit.test.ts + packages/objectql/src/registry.ts (`computeFQN`, `parseFQN`, `openObjectEntry`, `resolveObjectKey` / `getObject`, `registerObject`, `registerObjectExtension`, `assertSingleOwnerPerObject`), packages/objectql/src/engine.ts (the manifest `objectExtensions` loop, l. 9453), packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts (`saveMetaItem` gate order l. 21460 / 22148, `publishMetaItem` l. 24288, the `objectExtensionItemRefusal` host l. 7833, the `registrableObjectExtension` syncs), packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-authoring-gate.ts (`restoredBodyWriter`), packages/spec/src/kernel/customization-package.ts (`OVERRIDE_TYPE_CLASSIFICATION`), packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts (`ObjectExtensionSchema.extend`), docs/adr/0146 D6 / D10, packages/spec/src/kernel/metadata-plugin.zod.ts (the Wanted 2 row, read only). The changeset `.changeset/28834-object-extension-door-fit.md` is the prose face and is read for ②, not reviewed.

Rendered by the seat's subagent, reading the card (#28834, body and both comments), the PR (#28853 body, 4-file list, net diff `origin/main...461552ac`, merge-base `0c1829a2`) and the 48 check-runs on the head at 2026-11-02T01:35Z. The dispatching seat's own `Contract-review-claim:` comment was not an input. The dev's os-dev-report is read as the dev's account, never as the tree.

### Check-runs on the head (the gate verdicts)

48 check-runs, all `completed` at 2026-11-02T01:35Z; none in progress. 36 `success`, 12 `skipped` (UI build / type-check / lint / test shards, Build Docs, Dogfood Verify CLI, Temporal Conformance, the Dogfood Regression Gate shards, the Packed-tarball smoke, the 18.x upgrade harness opt-in, and the schedule gate: all path-filtered or opt-in), 0 `failure`. The gate families that decide: Check Changeset success, Governed Surface Queue Guard success, PR-body guards (claim · duplicate · Part-of · single-writer path) success, Lint & Repo Gates success (incl. Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · docs & code guards), Type Check · workspace / source gates / consumer gates / debt ledger success, Test Core 1/8 … 8/8 success, Dogfood Regression Gate success, Flag docs affected by code changes success. The dev's four local dogfood reds (the 18.0 upgrade-harness files) are on `main`, carried by #28849; the harness job is opt-in and skipped on this head, and no CI check-run is red.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Accept-set narrowing at the `object_extension` item doors — right.** `objectExtensionItemRefusal` step 4 now refuses, `VALIDATION_ERROR` / 400 with `issues[0].path === 'extend'`, a body whose `extend` resolves through `registry.getObject` to an object whose `name` differs from `extend`. Read in the cited code: `getObject` → `resolveObjectKey` answers the `objectKeysByShortName` index first (registry.ts l. 5942), which `openObjectEntry` fills with `parseFQN(fqn).shortName` (l. 3411), so a short name folds to a key only when that key carries `__` — a legacy `ns__name` key, exactly as the hunk claims. `registerObjectExtension` (l. 6095) hands `{ ...body, name: extend }` to `registerObject`, which files it under `computeFQN(namespace, schema.name)` — the identity (l. 472) — through `openObjectEntry(extend)`: the written spelling, never the folded one. So before this change the admitted write opened an owner-less `case` entry beside `crm__case`, and the fields never reached the target. Nothing refused that entry: `assertSingleOwnerPerObject` (l. 6189) has no caller under `packages/*/src` (CHANGELOG mentions only). The refusal lands on the three doors that already ask this one function — `saveMetaItem` (protocol.ts l. 22148, draft and publish alike), `publishMetaItem` on the draft promoted (l. 24288), and `restoredBodyWriter` (protocol-authoring-gate.ts l. 117). `publishPackageDrafts` does not ask it, and did not before: a draft of the folded spelling cannot exist, since the save door refuses it. The `typeof object.name === 'string'` guard keeps the gate's fail-open direction for a registry shape without a name.
2. **`declared_type_not_overridable` sentence for `object_extension` — right.** A branch keyed on `type === OBJECT_EXTENSION_TYPE`, placed after the `extend_only` (`object`) branch and before the generic `row?.disposition !== 'overridable'` D6 sentence. The spec classifies `object_extension` as `excluded` / `adr_0146_d10_extended` (customization-package.ts l. 341), so before this change it fell to the D6 sentence ("create your own object_extension under a new name"), which names a write the type cannot take: an extension's row name is its target (step 3 of the gate). Rule member, `NOT_OVERRIDABLE` / 403 and the `OverrideWriteRule` union are unchanged; only the message. Every other excluded type still reaches the D6 sentence (the permission control pins it byte for byte).
3. **`declared_object` sentence — right.** Message only; the rule and envelope stay. The sentence is also what `os validate` and the install door print (the docblock on `judgeOverrideWrite`), and it now names both the manifest entry and the item door `/api/v1/meta/object_extension`, which #28574 opened. No code or status changes anywhere.
4. **Public surface — none added.** `OBJECT_EXTENSION_ITEM_DOOR` is a module-private const. The new import of `OBJECT_EXTENSION_TYPE` into `protocol-packaged-base-refusal.ts` is acyclic (`protocol-object-extension-item.ts` imports nothing from it). No export, type, schema key, error code or gate is added; `packages/spec/**`, `computeFQN` and the `engine.ts` manifest loop are untouched, as the claim ruled.
5. **Not narrowed, and read as such — right by the claim, carried as a finding in ④.** The manifest `objectExtensions` loop (engine.ts l. 9455–9474) still registers `name: ext.extend` verbatim, and the boot / read hydrations register a stored row through `registrableObjectExtension` without this gate, so the same misfiling stays reachable through a code package's manifest and for a row already at rest. The PR body says so, and the claim's ⛔ excluded both.
6. **The test file — right.** Real `SqlDriver` + `ObjectQL` + protocol rig; the base ships `crm_account` and the legacy-keyed `crm__case`; the pair installs through `installPackage`. The override gate runs at `saveMetaItem` l. 21460 before the schema gate, so `overrides` on an `object_extension` body meets `judgeOverrideWrite` and not the strict parse's 422 — the sentences asserted are the ones the code emits (compared string by string against the hunks). The folded case is asserted in draft and publish-mode save with `issues` path, no row, no contributor under `case`, and the base's contributors unchanged; the registered-key control publishes and shows the pair as `extend` contributor with `region__c` folded in. The publish-of-a-stale-draft and restore arms of the same gate are not exercised here; they call the one function read above, so nothing is left unjudged.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/28834-object-extension-door-fit.md`: `"@objectstack/metadata-protocol": minor`, the `BREAKING` banner, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`, and the ADR-0087 `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` marker. This matches what the diff publishes: the only published package touched is `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` (the runtime file is a test, not a surface), one accept-set narrowing and two message changes, no schema key, no export. The repo's other `(narrowing)` changesets on `main` carry `patch` or `minor` with the `BREAKING` banner, never `major`, and the Check Changeset gate is green on this head, so `minor` is the convention's level. The `Clause-②:` line reads the same on the PR body and the changeset (`no (narrowing)`), and both carry `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`. The changeset's Before / Now / Who-sees-it paragraphs describe the diff I read, not more. The ADR-0087 reason holds: no key of any schema is added, removed, renamed or reshaped, and a row at rest is not rewritten, so there is nothing for a migration to carry.

Clause-②: no (narrowing) — read as declared, verified against the diff above.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **`open_questions` A vs B (keep `Fixes #28834` or narrow to `Refs`)** — answered: A. Wanted 1 and 3 land here; the seat carried Wanted 2 (the `object_extension` row comment in `packages/spec/src/kernel/metadata-plugin.zod.ts`, read at l. 807–828) to the spec lane as #28855, so closing the card loses nothing. Not counted as a gap of this PR.
- **Dev flag: no deployed store to read; a stored row of the folded spelling is not refused at rest** — answered, accepted. The hydrations never ask this gate (read in `registrableObjectExtension`'s callers), so such a row keeps opening its phantom entry silently on boot; its re-save, publish or restore is now refused with a sentence naming the registered key, and the author's path is delete the row and save it under that key. The measurement (the two shipped manifests extend their own keys; no non-test object named `ns__name` in this repo or hotcrm) is the dev's, and the tree shows the same two `extend` targets. Carried into ④ as a should-fix on the manifest and at-rest paths, not this PR's.
- **Dev flag: 4 dogfood reds in the 18.0 upgrade-harness files** — on `main`, carried by #28849; the CI harness job is opt-in and skipped on this head; the Dogfood Regression Gate and every Test Core shard are green. Not this diff.
- **Dev flag: PR #28811's body probe line `objects: []`** — prose on a merged PR; nothing in the tree to fix. Noted, no action.
- **The `declared_object` sentence names `/api/v1/meta/object_extension` even when printed by `os validate` or the install door** (manifest contexts with no running door) — the sentence names both places, so a manifest author still reads the manifest remedy first. Not escalated.

### ④ Design judgment

Judged against the published spec on `main`: `ObjectExtensionSchema.extend` is described as "Target object name (FQN) to extend" (object.zod.ts l. 4944), ADR-0146 D10 says an extension is "authored into `.custom`" and merged by `mergeObjectDefinitions` into the object it names, and the registry's own contract (`registerObjectExtension`'s docblock) is that `extend` "becomes the contribution's `name` (the object it registers under)".

- **Does the narrowing take a declared capability away at the consumer? No.** The spelling it refuses — a short name whose only match is a legacy `ns__name` key — was never a delivered capability at this door: the registry never folded it, so the write registered nothing on the target and opened an entry with no owner, which no invariant in the live tree checks. The spec's `extend` is the registered name, and the refusal makes the registry's own rule real at the write door, with a sentence that names the key to use. This is the right side of the line: a refusal of a write that never did what it said, not a narrowing of a delivered path.
- **Was implementing rather than refusing the better fit?** Folding at `registerObjectExtension` (resolve through `resolveObjectKey`) would deliver the write silently, but it would re-key a row stored under one name to another registry key, breaking step 3's "the row name is the target" and the one-extension-per-package-per-target identity the item door was built on (#28574), and leaving a GET that answers a different name than the registry serves. Refusal, as the card's Wanted 3 ordered, is the coherent choice. Not a finding.
- **Trying to break it.** (a) Ambiguous short name (two legacy keys sharing a short name): `resolveObjectKey` warns and returns the first; the refusal names that key — still a refusal, still a real key, and an author who meant the other reads the one-key sentence and writes the other key explicitly. Not a finding. (b) A tenant-authored owner (an `object` row) keyed by `body.name`: `name` equals the key, admitted as before. (c) Step order: the spelling check sits before the closure check (5), so a folded spelling outside the closure gets the spelling sentence first — the more actionable of the two. (d) The override branch order: `object` (`extend_only`) is judged before `object_extension`, and the new branch is keyed on the type constant rather than the classification row, so a future reclassification of `object_extension` would still route here; acceptable, since the sentence is about the type's nature (no new name), not its row. (e) The sentence change does not reach the generic D6 sentence for any other type — confirmed by the control and by reading the branch.
- **should-fix (carried, not this PR):** the same misfiling remains on the manifest path — `engine.ts` l. 9455 registers `name: ext.extend` verbatim for a code package's `objectExtensions` — and on the at-rest hydration of a stored row. A manifest with `extend: 'case'` against a legacy `crm__case` key passes `os validate` and the install door and opens the same phantom. The claim ⛔ excluded the manifest loop, and the card's Wanted 3 named the save gate only, so this is the objectql lane's own small card, with the same measurement (no shipped manifest or object reaches it today).

No must-fix.
